pr.title: test(composition): cover the catalog startup handoff
pr.body:
Register two regressions for the real signed AppHost validation-to-ordinary catalog handoff. The published validation process legitimately enriches the derived consumer-version cache. Reproducing the former unconditional materialization resets that cache and makes actual ordinary catalog generation refuse the invalidated proof; the published 1.4.1 path preserves the verified warm snapshot and generates the same catalog successfully.

The comparison allows only the actual CatalogBuilder consumer entry and its recomputed hash. Original source, pinned-tree, plan, existing snapshot fields, proof refusals and before-resource boundaries remain checked. The test fixture uses its existing inert image probe; it starts no services. Production source and the published 1.4.1 runtime are unchanged.

Validation: all 349 registered Release/package cases passed with no skips or errors; all 347 prior executed cases are retained. Exact signed tool members, 21,429 source hashes and 631 output DLLs remained unchanged through execution. First fixture and expectation failures are retained in the qualification evidence. Fresh PR/source gates remain required.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Test-only changes plus CI suite registration; production composition and published host behavior are exercised but not modified.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **regression coverage** for the transition from the real signed AppHost’s `--validate-platform` preflight through ordinary catalog generation, without starting services or mutating production code.
> 
> **`PlatformPartiesCatalogHandoffTests`** runs published validation with a registry-free docker probe that is allowed to finish the catalog phase (`completeCatalog: true`), then asserts preflight legitimately warms `catalog-versions.json` (only a derived **CatalogBuilder** consumer entry and its hash). A parameterized follow-on exercises ordinary composition: the **1.4.1** materialization path keeps that warm snapshot, proof still matches, and generated `catalog.json` matches preflight; the legacy **1.4.0** unconditional rematerialization resets the snapshot, invalidates the qualified runner proof, and catalog generation fails with the expected refusal—all while other authority inputs and pinned-tree bytes stay unchanged.
> 
> **`PlatformPartiesPackageFixture.RunPublishedValidationAsync`** gains an optional `completeCatalog` flag (default preserves existing early-stop behavior for other tests) that drops the seventh-image probe exit so validation can reach catalog completion.
> 
> **`eng/tuple-ci-suites.json`** registers the new class for **2** required CI cases (the theory’s two inline scenarios).
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 6e1a04d3a24ebe7a93fb6794b1ceec29d57aa445. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
